messages.subject: CXXR and Pyston
messages.body_plain:
Pyston (https://github.com/dropbox/pyston) is a project supported by
DropBox to implement a fast python VM on top of LLVM using modern JIT
techniques.

As such, they either have or will implement a lot of the things that
we need to JIT scalar R code -- including dynamic type specialization,
OSR entry and exit, auto-unboxing, multiple performance tiers etc.

>From a superficial look at the code, the overall design seems very
similar to what we're doing -- translating functions directly from an
AST representation to LLVM IR and then running both their own
python-specific high-level optimization passes and LLVM's low-level
ones on top of that.

I'm going to investigate modifying the CXXR JIT to use the pyston code
generation code as much as possible.  It may save a lot of effort.

messages.subject: Re: CXXR and Pyston
messages.body_plain:
This is cool -- though I would probably want to retain our own implementation.
There are many differences between the two languages, buying into their design
choice may force us to do things in a way that is not natural for R.

We can surely reuse code though.

-jan

Jan Vitek, Professor
Computer Science,
Northeastern University
